The statute described is Section 274A of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), specifically the employer sanctions provision. Its primary legal implication is that it imposes civil and criminal liability on employers who knowingly hire, recruit, or refer for a fee individuals who are not authorized to work in the United States. To comply, employers must verify the identity and employment authorization of all employees hired after November 6, 1986, using Form I-9. Failure to do so, or hiring individuals known to be unauthorized, can result in substantial civil fines per unauthorized worker, and in cases of pattern or practice violations or aggravated circumstances, criminal penalties including imprisonment.
